    66→class SessionCostTracker:
    67→    """Per-session cost accumulator with non-blocking async flush.
    68→
    69→    Design principles:
    70→    - Hot path: <0.05ms (in-memory tracking only)
    71→    - Batch flushes: 100 records/batch, async (non-blocking)
    72→    - Vault failures: Gracefully degrade to in-memory tracking
    73→    - Accuracy: ±1% (cost calculations include rounding)
    74→    """
    75→
    76→    _current_instance: ClassVar[Optional["SessionCostTracker"]] = None
    77→    _lock: ClassVar[threading.Lock] = threading.Lock()
    78→
    79→    def __init__(
    80→        self,
    81→        session_id: str,
    82→        model_costs: dict[str, float] | None = None,
    83→        batch_size: int = 100,
    84→        vault_logger=None,
    85→    ):
    86→        """Initialize cost tracker.
    87→
    88→        Args:
    89→            session_id: Unique session identifier
    90→            model_costs: Dict mapping model names to cost per 1K tokens (default: standard rates)
    91→            batch_size: Records to batch before flushing (default: 100)
    92→            vault_logger: Optional vault persistence logger (non-blocking)
    93→        """
    94→        self.session_id = session_id
    95→        self.batch_size = batch_size
    96→        self.vault_logger = vault_logger
    97→
    98→        # Standard API costs (per 1K tokens)
    99→        # Local models (ollama) = $0.00
   100→        # API models: conservative estimates for unknown models
   101→        self.model_costs = model_costs or {
   102→            # Local models
   103→            "phi3:mini": 0.0,
   104→            "gemma3:4b": 0.0,
   105→            "mistral:7b": 0.0,
   106→            "llama4-scout": 0.0,
   107→            "qwen3-coder:32b": 0.0,
   108→            "deepseek-r1:8b": 0.0,
   109→            # API models (conservative estimates)
   110→            "gpt-4": 0.03,  # $0.03 per 1K tokens (input)
   111→            "gpt-4o": 0.015,  # $0.015 per 1K tokens
   112→            "claude-3-opus": 0.015,  # $0.015 per 1K tokens (input)
   113→            "claude-3-sonnet": 0.003,  # $0.003 per 1K tokens
   114→            "claude-3-haiku": 0.00025,  # $0.00025 per 1K tokens
   115→        }
   116→
   117→        # In-memory tracking (hot path)
   118→        self.records: list[CostRecord] = []
   119→        self.total_tokens = 0
   120→        self.total_cost_usd = 0.0
   121→        self.model_usage: dict[str, int] = {}
   122→        self.start_time = time.time()
   123→
   124→        # Flush state
   125→        self._flush_task: asyncio.Task | None = None
   126→        self._pending_flush = False
   127→        self._background_tasks: set[asyncio.Task] = set()
   128→
   129→    @classmethod
   130→    def get_current(cls) -> Optional["SessionCostTracker"]:
   131→        """Get current session tracker (thread-safe)."""
   132→        return cls._current_instance
   133→
   134→    @classmethod
   135→    def set_current(cls, tracker: Optional["SessionCostTracker"]) -> None:
   136→        """Set current session tracker (thread-safe)."""
   137→        cls._current_instance = tracker
   138→
   139→    def track_usage_fast(
   140→        self,
   141→        model: str,
   142→        tokens: int,
   143→        duration_ms: float = 0.0,
   144→    ) -> float:
   145→        """Track usage in hot path (<0.05ms).
   146→
   147→        Args:
   148→            model: Model name
   149→            tokens: Tokens used
   150→            duration_ms: Request duration (optional, for analytics)
   151→
   152→        Returns:
   153→            Estimated cost in USD
   154→        """
   155→        # Calculate cost (in-memory, O(1))
   156→        cost_per_1k = self.model_costs.get(model, 0.015)  # Conservative default
   157→        cost_usd = (tokens / 1000.0) * cost_per_1k
   158→
   159→        # Record (in-memory, O(1) amortized)
   160→        record = CostRecord(
   161→            timestamp=time.time(),
   162→            session_id=self.session_id,
   163→            model=model,
   164→            tokens=tokens,
   165→            duration_ms=duration_ms,
   166→            cost_usd=cost_usd,
   167→        )
   168→        self.records.append(record)
   169→
   170→        # Accumulate totals (O(1))
   171→        self.total_tokens += tokens
   172→        self.total_cost_usd += cost_usd
   173→        self.model_usage[model] = self.model_usage.get(model, 0) + tokens
   174→
   175→        # Check if batch is ready for flush (non-blocking)
   176→        if len(self.records) >= self.batch_size and not self._pending_flush:
   177→            self._schedule_flush()
   178→
   179→        return cost_usd
   180→
   181→    def _schedule_flush(self) -> None:
   182→        """Schedule asynchronous flush (non-blocking, best-effort)."""
   183→        self._pending_flush = True
   184→        try:
   185→            # Only schedule if event loop is running
   186→            loop = asyncio.get_event_loop()
   187→            if loop.is_running():
   188→                _task = loop.create_task(self._flush_batch())
   189→                self._background_tasks.add(_task)
   190→                _task.add_done_callback(self._background_tasks.discard)
   191→            else:
   192→                # Fallback: synchronous flush (shouldn't happen in async context)
   193→                self._flush_batch_sync()
   194→        except RuntimeError:
   195→            # No event loop running, fall back to sync
   196→            self._flush_batch_sync()
   197→
   198→    async def _flush_batch(self) -> None:
   199→        """Asynchronous batch flush (non-blocking)."""
   200→        if not self.records:
   201→            self._pending_flush = False
   202→            return
   203→
   204→        # Take snapshot (minimal lock time)
   205→        records_to_flush = self.records[: self.batch_size]
   206→        remaining = self.records[self.batch_size :]
   207→
   208→        try:
   209→            # Attempt vault persistence (best-effort, non-blocking)
   210→            if self.vault_logger:
   211→                try:
   212→                    # Non-blocking vault write (timeout + exception handling)
   213→                    await asyncio.wait_for(
   214→                        self.vault_logger.log_cost_records(records_to_flush),
   215→                        timeout=5.0,
   216→                    )
   217→                    # Success: remove flushed records
   218→                    self.records[:] = remaining
   219→                except (TimeoutError, Exception) as e:
   220→                    # Vault failure: keep records in-memory
   221→                    logger.warning(
   222→                        f"Cost tracking vault flush failed: {e}. Keeping {len(records_to_flush)} records in memory."
   223→                    )
   224→        finally:
   225→            self._pending_flush = False
   226→
   227→    def _flush_batch_sync(self) -> None:
   228→        """Synchronous fallback for flush (shouldn't be used normally)."""
   229→        if not self.records:
   230→            return
   231→
   232→        records_to_flush = self.records[: self.batch_size]
   233→        logger.debug(f"Cost tracker: Synchronous flush of {len(records_to_flush)} records")
   234→        # In sync context, just log locally. Records stay in memory.
   235→        self._pending_flush = False
   236→
   237→    async def flush_all(self) -> int:
   238→        """Flush all remaining records to vault.
   239→
   240→        Returns:
   241→            Number of records flushed
   242→        """
   243→        if not self.records:
   244→            return 0
   245→
   246→        records_to_flush = self.records[:]
   247→        flushed_count = 0
   248→
   249→        try:
   250→            if self.vault_logger:
   251→                # Flush in batches
   252→                for i in range(0, len(records_to_flush), self.batch_size):
   253→                    batch = records_to_flush[i : i + self.batch_size]
   254→                    try:
   255→                        await asyncio.wait_for(
   256→                            self.vault_logger.log_cost_records(batch),
   257→                            timeout=5.0,
   258→                        )
   259→                        flushed_count += len(batch)
   260→                    except (TimeoutError, Exception) as e:
   261→                        logger.warning(f"Batch flush failed: {e}")
   262→                        break
   263→
   264→        finally:
   265→            # Remove successfully flushed records
   266→            if flushed_count > 0:
   267→                self.records = self.records[flushed_count:]
   268→
   269→        return flushed_count
   270→
   271→    def get_session_cost(self) -> dict:
   272→        """Get session cost summary.
   273→
   274→        Returns:
   275→            Dictionary with total_cost_usd, total_tokens, model_usage, duration_sec
   276→        """
   277→        return {
   278→            "total_cost_usd": self.total_cost_usd,
   279→            "total_tokens": self.total_tokens,
   280→            "model_usage": self.model_usage.copy(),
   281→            "duration_sec": time.time() - self.start_time,
   282→            "pending_records": len(self.records),
   283→        }
   284→
   285→    def reset(self) -> None:
   286→        """Reset tracker (for testing)."""
   287→        self.records.clear()
   288→        self.total_tokens = 0
   289→        self.total_cost_usd = 0.0
   290→        self.model_usage.clear()
   291→
   292→
   293→def get_current_tracker() -> SessionCostTracker | None:
   294→    """Get current session cost tracker."""
   295→    return SessionCostTracker.get_current()
   296→
   297→
   298→def set_current_tracker(tracker: SessionCostTracker | None) -> None:
   299→    """Set current session cost tracker."""
   300→    SessionCostTracker.set_current(tracker)
   301→
   302→
   303→def reset_current_tracker() -> None:
   304→    """Reset current session tracker (testing only)."""
   305→    SessionCostTracker.set_current(None)
   306→

   108→    async def sync_journey(self, task_file: str, plan_file: str) -> bool:
   109→        """Synchronize the current development journey (tasks and plans) to memory.
   110→
   111→        Args:
   112→            task_file: Path to task.md artifact.
   113→            plan_file: Path to implementation_plan.md artifact.
   114→
   115→        Returns:
   116→            True if synchronized successfully.
   117→        """
   118→        import os
   119→        from datetime import datetime
   120→
   121→        try:
   122→            # Read artifacts
   123→            with open(task_file) as f:
   124→                task_content = f.read()
   125→            with open(plan_file) as f:
   126→                plan_content = f.read()
   127→
   128→            # Format for MISSION_JOURNAL.md
   129→            date_str = datetime.now().strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
   130→            journal_entry = f"\n\n## Session Developments ({date_str})\n"
   131→            journal_entry += (
   132→                f"- **Targeted Mission State**: Synchronized journey from "
   133→                f"`{os.path.basename(task_file)}` and `{os.path.basename(plan_file)}`.\n"
   134→            )
   135→
   136→            # Extract key milestones (simple heuristic)
   137→            for line in task_content.split("\n"):
   138→                if line.strip().startswith("- [x]"):
   139→                    milestone = line.replace("- [x]", "").strip()
   140→                    journal_entry += f"- **Accomplishment**: {milestone}\n"
   141→
   142→            journal_path = "src/cohezion/knowledge_graph/MISSION_JOURNAL.md"
   143→            with open(journal_path, "a") as f:
   144→                f.write(journal_entry)
   145→
   146→            # Store in SurrealDB as a high-fidelity state node
   147→            node = KnowledgeNode(
   148→                concept=f"Journey Sync {date_str}",
   149→                node_type="journey_snapshot",
   150→                metadata={
   151→                    "tasks": task_content,
   152→                    "plan": plan_content,
   153→                    "timestamp": datetime.now().isoformat(),
   154→                },
   155→            )
   156→            await self.add_node(node)
   157→
   158→            logger.info(f"✅ Journey synchronized to {journal_path} and SurrealDB.")
   159→            return True
   160→
   161→        except Exception as e:
   162→            logger.error(f"Failed to sync journey: {e}")
   163→            return False

   165→    async def add_edge(self, edge: KnowledgeEdge) -> str:

   189→    async def query_concept(
   190→        self,
   191→        concept: str,
   192→        limit: int = 10,
   193→    ) -> KnowledgeQuery:
   194→        """Query the knowledge graph for a concept.
   195→
   196→        Args:
   197→            concept: Concept to search for.
   198→            limit: Maximum results.
   199→
   200→        Returns:
   201→            KnowledgeQuery with matches.
   202→        """
   203→        try:
   204→            similar_nodes = await self._universe_repo.query_similar(
   205→                vector=self._concept_to_vector(concept),
   206→                limit=limit,
   207→                node_type="kg_concept",
   208→            )
   209→
   210→            matched_nodes = [
   211→                KnowledgeNode(
   212→                    id=node.id,
   213→                    concept=node.content,
   214→                    node_type=node.node_type.replace("kg_", ""),
   215→                    metadata=node.metadata,
   216→                    created_at=node.created_at.isoformat(),
   217→                    embedding=node.embedding,
   218→                )
   219→                for node in similar_nodes
   220→            ]
   221→
   222→            matched_edges = []
   223→
   224→            for node in matched_nodes:
   225→                edges = await self._universe_repo.get_relationships(
   226→                    node.id,
   227→                    direction="both",
   228→                )
   229→                matched_edges.extend(edges)
   230→
   231→            confidence = len(matched_nodes) / limit if matched_nodes else 0.0
   232→
   233→            return KnowledgeQuery(
   234→                matched_nodes=matched_nodes,
   235→                matched_edges=matched_edges,
   236→                confidence=confidence,
   237→                path=[n.id for n in matched_nodes],
   238→            )
   239→
   240→        except Exception as e:
   241→            logger.error(f"Failed to query concept: {e}")
   242→            return KnowledgeQuery(
   243→                matched_nodes=[],
   244→                matched_edges=[],
   245→                confidence=0.0,
   246→            )

   363→    async def find_related_skills(
   364→        self,
   365→        skill_name: str,
   366→        limit: int = 5,
   367→    ) -> list[Skill]:
   368→        """Find skills related to a given skill.
   369→
   370→        Args:
   371→            skill_name: Name of reference skill.
   372→            limit: Maximum results.
   373→
   374→        Returns:
   375→            List of related skills.
   376→        """
   377→        try:
   378→            skill = await self._skill_repo.get_by_name(skill_name)
   379→            if not skill:
   380→                return []
   381→
   382→            concept_query = await self.query_concept(
   383→                skill.description,
   384→                limit=limit * 2,
   385→            )
   386→
   387→            related_skill_names = set()
   388→            for node in concept_query.matched_nodes:
   389→                name = node.metadata.get("name")
   390→                if name and name != skill_name:
   391→                    related_skill_names.add(name)
   392→
   393→            related_skills = []
   394→            for name in list(related_skill_names)[:limit]:
   395→                s = await self._skill_repo.get_by_name(name)
   396→                if s:
   397→                    related_skills.append(s)
   398→
   399→            return related_skills
   400→
   401→        except Exception as e:
   402→            logger.error(f"Failed to find related skills: {e}")
   403→            return []

   405→    async def get_graph_statistics(self) -> dict[str, int]:
   406→        """Get statistics about the knowledge graph.
   407→
   408→        Returns:
   409→            Dictionary with node and edge counts.
   410→        """
   411→        try:
   412→            concept_count = await self._universe_repo.count(node_type="kg_concept")
   413→            skill_count = await self._universe_repo.count(node_type="kg_skill")
   414→            total_nodes = await self._universe_repo.count()
   415→
   416→            return {
   417→                "concept_nodes": concept_count,
   418→                "skill_nodes": skill_count,
   419→                "total_nodes": total_nodes,
   420→            }
   421→
   422→        except Exception as e:
   423→            logger.error(f"Failed to get graph statistics: {e}")

   425→                "concept_nodes": 0,
   426→                "skill_nodes": 0,
   427→                "total_nodes": 0,
   428→            }

   430→    async def _bfs_find_path(
   431→        self,
   432→        from_id: str,
   433→        to_id: str,
   434→        max_depth: int,
   435→    ) -> list[str]:
   436→        """BFS to find path between nodes.
   437→
   438→        Args:
   439→            from_id: Starting node ID.
   440→            to_id: Target node ID.
   441→            max_depth: Maximum search depth.
   442→
   443→        Returns:
   444→            List of node IDs in path.
   445→        """
   446→        from collections import deque
   447→
   448→        queue = deque([(from_id, [from_id])])
   449→        visited = {from_id}
   450→
   451→        while queue:
   452→            current_id, path = queue.popleft()
   453→
   454→            if current_id == to_id:
   455→                return path
   456→
   457→            if len(path) >= max_depth:
   458→                continue
   459→
   460→            edges = await self._universe_repo.get_relationships(
   461→                current_id,
   462→                direction="both",
   463→            )
   464→
   465→            for edge in edges:
   466→                neighbor = edge.get("to") if edge.get("from") == current_id else edge.get("from")
   467→                if neighbor and neighbor not in visited:
   468→                    visited.add(neighbor)
   469→                    queue.append((neighbor, [*path, neighbor]))
   470→
   471→        return []
   472→
   473→    def _concept_to_vector(self, concept: str) -> list[float]:
   474→        """Convert concept string to a simple vector."""
   475→        import hashlib
   476→
   477→        # Security: SHA-256 used for deterministic vector generation (non-security purpose)
   478→        hash_obj = hashlib.sha256(concept.encode())
   479→        hash_bytes = hash_obj.digest()
   480→
   481→        vector = [float(b) / 255.0 for b in hash_bytes[:32]]
   482→
   483→        while len(vector) < 768:
   484→            vector.append(0.0)
   485→
   486→        return vector[:768]
   487→

1→"""Cost trend forecasting engine for predictive analytics.
     2→
     3→Provides:
     4→- Time-series forecasting (24h, 7d, 30d horizons)
     5→- Exponential smoothing and trend analysis
     6→- Confidence intervals for forecasts
     7→- Anomaly scoring for unusual spend patterns
     8→"""
     9→
    10→from __future__ import annotations
    11→
    12→import logging
    13→import math
    14→import time
    15→from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass
    16→from typing import Any
    17→
    18→
    19→logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    20→
    21→
    22→@dataclass
    23→class Forecast:
    24→    """Single cost forecast point."""
    25→
    26→    timestamp: float
    27→    horizon_hours: int
    28→    predicted_cost_usd: float

    43→    timestamp: float

    45→    forecast_7d_usd: float
    46→    forecast_30d_usd: float
    47→    confidence_24h: float

    59→class AnomalyScore:
    60→    """Anomaly detection result for spend pattern."""
    61→
    62→    timestamp: float
    63→    current_rate_usd_per_hour: float
    64→    expected_rate_usd_per_hour: float
    65→    deviation_pct: float
    66→    anomaly_score: float  # 0-100, higher = more anomalous
    67→    is_anomaly: bool  # True if deviation > threshold (default: >20%)
    68→    anomaly_type: str  # "spike", "drop", "trend_change", "normal"

    71→        """Convert to dictionary."""

    74→
    75→class ForecastEngine:
    76→    """Cost trend forecasting with anomaly detection."""
    77→
    78→    def __init__(
    79→        self,
    80→        alpha: float = 0.3,  # Exponential smoothing parameter
    81→        anomaly_threshold_pct: float = 20.0,  # % deviation for anomaly
    82→    ):
    83→        """Initialize forecast engine.
    84→
    85→        Args:
    86→            alpha: Smoothing factor for exponential smoothing (0-1)
    87→            anomaly_threshold_pct: Percentage deviation threshold for anomaly detection
    88→        """
    89→        self.alpha = alpha
    90→        self.anomaly_threshold_pct = anomaly_threshold_pct
    91→
    92→        # Historical data: (timestamp, cost_usd, hour_duration)
    93→        self.history: list[tuple[float, float, float]] = []
    94→        self.smoothed_level = 0.0
    95→        self.smoothed_trend = 0.0
    96→
    97→    def add_observation(
    98→        self,
    99→        timestamp: float,
   100→        cost_usd: float,
   101→        duration_hours: float = 1.0,
   102→    ) -> None:
   103→        """Add historical cost observation.
   104→
   105→        Args:
   106→            timestamp: Observation timestamp
   107→            cost_usd: Cost in USD
   108→            duration_hours: Duration of measurement in hours
   109→        """
   110→        self.history.append((timestamp, cost_usd, duration_hours))
   111→
   112→        # Update smoothed estimates
   113→        if len(self.history) == 1:
   114→            self.smoothed_level = cost_usd / duration_hours
   115→            self.smoothed_trend = 0.0
   116→        else:
   117→            # Simple exponential smoothing with trend
   118→            previous_level = self.smoothed_level
   119→            current_rate = cost_usd / duration_hours
   120→
   121→            new_level = self.alpha * current_rate + (1 - self.alpha) * previous_level
   122→            new_trend = self.alpha * (new_level - previous_level)
   123→
   124→            self.smoothed_level = new_level
   125→            self.smoothed_trend = new_trend
   126→
   127→    def forecast(
   128→        self,
   129→        horizon_hours: int,
   130→        confidence_pct: float = 90.0,
   131→    ) -> Forecast | None:
   132→        """Generate forecast for given horizon.
   133→
   134→        Args:
   135→            horizon_hours: Number of hours to forecast ahead
   136→            confidence_pct: Confidence level for interval (90 or 95)
   137→
   138→        Returns:
   139→            Forecast object or None if insufficient data
   140→        """
   141→        if len(self.history) < 2:
   142→            return None
   143→
   144→        # Use exponential smoothing for forecast
   145→        forecast_value = self.smoothed_level + (horizon_hours / 24.0) * self.smoothed_trend
   146→
   147→        # Confidence interval (simplified: ±10-20% depending on horizon)
   148→        interval_width = forecast_value * (0.10 + 0.05 * math.log(horizon_hours + 1))
   149→
   150→        lower = max(0, forecast_value - interval_width)
   151→        upper = forecast_value + interval_width
   152→
   153→        return Forecast(
   154→            timestamp=time.time(),
   155→            horizon_hours=horizon_hours,
   156→            predicted_cost_usd=forecast_value * horizon_hours,
   157→            confidence_interval_lower=lower * horizon_hours,
   158→            confidence_interval_upper=upper * horizon_hours,
   159→            confidence_pct=confidence_pct,
   160→            method="exponential_smoothing",
   161→        )
   162→
   163→    def forecast_summary(self) -> ForecastSummary | None:
   164→        """Get forecasts for standard time horizons.
   165→
   166→        Returns:
   167→            ForecastSummary or None if insufficient data
   168→        """
   169→        if len(self.history) < 2:
   170→            return None
   171→
   172→        forecast_24h = self.forecast(24)
   173→        forecast_7d = self.forecast(7 * 24)
   174→        forecast_30d = self.forecast(30 * 24)
   175→
   176→        if not forecast_24h:
   177→            return None
   178→
   179→        # Determine trend
   180→        trend_direction = "stable"
   181→        if self.smoothed_trend > 0.01:
   182→            trend_direction = "increasing"
   183→        elif self.smoothed_trend < -0.01:
   184→            trend_direction = "decreasing"
   185→
   186→        return ForecastSummary(
   187→            timestamp=time.time(),
   188→            forecast_24h_usd=forecast_24h.predicted_cost_usd,
   189→            forecast_7d_usd=forecast_7d.predicted_cost_usd if forecast_7d else 0.0,
   190→            forecast_30d_usd=forecast_30d.predicted_cost_usd if forecast_30d else 0.0,
   191→            confidence_24h=forecast_24h.confidence_pct,
   192→            confidence_7d=forecast_7d.confidence_pct if forecast_7d else 90.0,
   193→            confidence_30d=forecast_30d.confidence_pct if forecast_30d else 90.0,
   194→            trend_direction=trend_direction,
   195→            forecast_method="exponential_smoothing",
   196→        )
   197→
   198→    def detect_anomaly(
   199→        self,
   200→        current_rate_usd_per_hour: float,
   201→    ) -> AnomalyScore:
   202→        """Detect anomalies in current spend rate.
   203→
   204→        Args:
   205→            current_rate_usd_per_hour: Current spend rate in USD/hour
   206→
   207→        Returns:
   208→            AnomalyScore with anomaly detection result
   209→        """
   210→        expected_rate = self.smoothed_level
   211→        deviation = abs(current_rate_usd_per_hour - expected_rate)
   212→        deviation_pct = (deviation / expected_rate * 100) if expected_rate > 0 else 0
   213→
   214→        # Anomaly scoring: 0-100
   215→        # 0 = no deviation, 50 = 20% threshold, 100 = 50% deviation
   216→        anomaly_score = min(100, (deviation_pct / 50) * 100)
   217→
   218→        is_anomaly = deviation_pct > self.anomaly_threshold_pct
   219→
   220→        # Determine anomaly type
   221→        anomaly_type = "normal"
   222→        if is_anomaly:
   223→            anomaly_type = "spike" if current_rate_usd_per_hour > expected_rate else "drop"
   224→
   225→        return AnomalyScore(
   226→            timestamp=time.time(),
   227→            current_rate_usd_per_hour=current_rate_usd_per_hour,
   228→            expected_rate_usd_per_hour=expected_rate,
   229→            deviation_pct=deviation_pct,
   230→            anomaly_score=anomaly_score,
   231→            is_anomaly=is_anomaly,
   232→            anomaly_type=anomaly_type,
   233→        )
   234→
   235→    def get_history_stats(self) -> dict[str, float]:
   236→        """Get statistics from historical data.
   237→
   238→        Returns:
   239→            Dictionary with min, max, mean, and trend stats
   240→        """
   241→        if not self.history:
   242→            return {}
   243→
   244→        costs = [cost for _, cost, duration in self.history]
   245→        rates = [cost / duration for _, cost, duration in self.history]
   246→
   247→        return {
   248→            "min_rate_usd_per_hour": min(rates) if rates else 0,
   249→            "max_rate_usd_per_hour": max(rates) if rates else 0,
   250→            "mean_rate_usd_per_hour": sum(rates) / len(rates) if rates else 0,
   251→            "total_cost_usd": sum(costs),
   252→            "observation_count": len(self.history),
   253→            "smoothed_level_usd_per_hour": self.smoothed_level,
   254→            "smoothed_trend_usd_per_hour": self.smoothed_trend,
   255→        }
   256→
   257→    def reset(self) -> None:
   258→        """Reset forecast engine (testing only)."""
   259→        self.history.clear()
   260→        self.smoothed_level = 0.0
   261→        self.smoothed_trend = 0.0
   262→
   263→
   264→_instance: ForecastEngine | None = None
   265→
   266→
   267→def get_forecast_engine() -> ForecastEngine:
   268→    """Get or create singleton forecast engine."""
   269→    global _instance
   270→    if _instance is None:
   271→        _instance = ForecastEngine()
   272→    return _instance
   273→
   274→
   275→def reset_forecast_engine() -> None:
   276→    """Reset forecast engine singleton (testing only)."""
   277→    global _instance
   278→    _instance = None

1→"""Budget enforcement with soft-stop policy and emergency circuit breaker.
     2→
     3→Features:
     4→- Per-session budget limits with configurable thresholds
     5→- Soft-stop policy: Finish current task, block new ones
     6→- Progressive cost alerts: 80%, 90%, 95%, 100%
     7→- Circuit breaker: 3-strike emergency shutoff
     8→- Cached budget checks (60s refresh, <0.5ms critical path)
     9→- Non-blocking async persistence (best-effort)
    10→
    11→Architecture:
    12→  Budget Check (cached)
    13→       ↓
    14→  Threshold evaluation (80%, 90%, 95%, 100%)
    15→       ↓
    16→  Alert/Block (based on policy)
    17→       ↓
    18→  Circuit Breaker (3-strike emergency)
    19→
    20→Usage:
    21→    enforcer = BudgetEnforcer(
    22→        budget_usd=10.0,
    23→        warn_threshold_pct=80,
    24→        critical_threshold_pct=90,
    25→        block_threshold_pct=100,
    26→    )
    27→
    28→    can_proceed, reason = enforcer.check_budget(current_cost_usd=8.5)
    29→    if not can_proceed:
    30→        logger.warning(f"Budget enforcement: {reason}")
    31→        # Soft-stop: Block new tasks, allow current to finish
    32→"""
    33→
    34→import asyncio
    35→import logging
    36→import time
    37→from dataclasses import dataclass
    38→from enum import Enum
    39→from typing import ClassVar, Optional
    40→
    41→
    42→logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    43→
    44→
    45→class BudgetPolicy(Enum):
    46→    """Budget enforcement policy."""
    47→
    48→    SOFT_STOP = "soft_stop"  # Finish current task, block new ones
    49→    HARD_STOP = "hard_stop"  # Immediate stop (not recommended)
    50→    WARNING_ONLY = "warning_only"  # Just log alerts, don't block
    51→
    52→
    53→@dataclass
    54→class BudgetState:
    55→    """Budget enforcement state snapshot."""
    56→
    57→    total_budget_usd: float
    58→    current_cost_usd: float
    59→    remaining_budget_usd: float
    60→    utilization_pct: float
    61→    status: str  # "OK", "WARNING", "CRITICAL", "BLOCKED"
    62→    last_check_time: float
    63→    alert_count: int = 0
    64→
    65→    def to_dict(self) -> dict:
    66→        """Convert to dictionary."""
    67→        return {
    68→            "total_budget_usd": self.total_budget_usd,
    69→            "current_cost_usd": self.current_cost_usd,
    70→            "remaining_budget_usd": self.remaining_budget_usd,
    71→            "utilization_pct": self.utilization_pct,
    72→            "status": self.status,
    73→            "last_check_time": self.last_check_time,
    74→            "alert_count": self.alert_count,
    75→        }
    76→
    77→
    78→class CostAlertManager:
    79→    """Manages cost alerts at different thresholds."""
    80→
    81→    def __init__(
    82→        self,
    83→        warn_threshold_pct: int = 80,
    84→        critical_threshold_pct: int = 90,
    85→        extreme_threshold_pct: int = 95,
    86→    ):
    87→        """Initialize alert manager.
    88→
    89→        Args:
    90→            warn_threshold_pct: Warning threshold percentage (default: 80%)
    91→            critical_threshold_pct: Critical threshold percentage (default: 90%)
    92→            extreme_threshold_pct: Extreme threshold percentage (default: 95%)
    93→        """
    94→        self.warn_threshold = warn_threshold_pct
    95→        self.critical_threshold = critical_threshold_pct
    96→        self.extreme_threshold = extreme_threshold_pct
    97→
    98→        # Track alerts to avoid spamming
    99→        self.last_warn_time = 0.0
   100→        self.last_critical_time = 0.0
   101→        self.alert_count = 0
   102→        self.alert_cooldown_sec = 60  # Don't spam alerts more than once/min
   103→
   104→    def evaluate(self, utilization_pct: float) -> tuple[str, str | None]:
   105→        """Evaluate utilization and return status + optional alert.
   106→
   107→        Args:
   108→            utilization_pct: Budget utilization percentage (0-100+)
   109→
   110→        Returns:
   111→            Tuple of (status, alert_message)
   112→            - status: "OK", "WARNING", "CRITICAL", "EXTREME", "BLOCKED"
   113→            - alert_message: Alert message if threshold crossed, else None
   114→        """
   115→        current_time = time.time()
   116→
   117→        if utilization_pct < self.warn_threshold:
   118→            return "OK", None
   119→
   120→        if utilization_pct < self.critical_threshold:
   121→            if current_time - self.last_warn_time > self.alert_cooldown_sec:
   122→                self.last_warn_time = current_time
   123→                self.alert_count += 1
   124→                msg = f"Cost WARNING: Budget utilization at {utilization_pct:.1f}% (threshold: {self.warn_threshold}%)"
   125→                return "WARNING", msg
   126→            return "WARNING", None
   127→
   128→        if utilization_pct < self.extreme_threshold:
   129→            if current_time - self.last_critical_time > self.alert_cooldown_sec:
   130→                self.last_critical_time = current_time
   131→                self.alert_count += 1
   132→                msg = (
   133→                    f"Cost CRITICAL: Budget utilization at {utilization_pct:.1f}% "
   134→                    f"(threshold: {self.critical_threshold}%)"
   135→                )
   136→                return "CRITICAL", msg
   137→            return "CRITICAL", None
   138→
   139→        if utilization_pct < 100.0:
   140→            msg = f"Cost EXTREME: Budget utilization at {utilization_pct:.1f}% (threshold: {self.extreme_threshold}%)"
   141→            return "EXTREME", msg
   142→
   143→        return "BLOCKED", f"Budget limit reached ({utilization_pct:.1f}%)"
   144→

   146→class BudgetCircuitBreaker:
   147→    """Emergency circuit breaker for runaway costs.
   148→
   149→    Implements 3-strike rule: 3 policy violations trigger emergency shutoff.
   150→    """
   151→
   152→    def __init__(self, strike_limit: int = 3):
   153→        """Initialize circuit breaker.
   154→
   155→        Args:
   156→            strike_limit: Number of violations before opening (default: 3)
   157→        """
   158→        self.strike_limit = strike_limit
   159→        self.strike_count = 0
   160→        self.is_open = False
   161→        self.open_time = 0.0
   162→        self.reset_timeout_sec = 300  # Auto-reset after 5 minutes
   163→
   164→    def record_violation(self) -> bool:
   165→        """Record a policy violation.
   166→
   167→        Returns:
   168→            True if circuit breaker opened, False otherwise
   169→        """
   170→        self.strike_count += 1
   171→        logger.warning(f"Budget violation recorded: {self.strike_count}/{self.strike_limit}")
   172→
   173→        if self.strike_count >= self.strike_limit:
   174→            self.is_open = True
   175→            self.open_time = time.time()
   176→            logger.error(
   177→                f"Budget circuit breaker OPENED after {self.strike_count} violations. "
   178→                "Blocking all operations until manual reset or timeout."
   179→            )
   180→            return True
   181→
   182→        return False
   183→
   184→    def check_state(self) -> bool:
   185→        """Check if circuit breaker is currently open.
   186→
   187→        Returns:
   188→            True if open, False if closed or auto-reset
   189→        """
   190→        if not self.is_open:
   191→            return False
   192→
   193→        # Check if auto-reset timeout elapsed
   194→        if time.time() - self.open_time > self.reset_timeout_sec:
   195→            logger.info(f"Budget circuit breaker auto-reset after {self.reset_timeout_sec}s")
   196→            self.is_open = False
   197→            self.strike_count = 0
   198→            return False
   199→
   200→        return True
   201→
   202→    def reset(self) -> None:
   203→        """Manually reset circuit breaker."""
   204→        logger.info("Budget circuit breaker manually reset")
   205→        self.is_open = False
   206→        self.strike_count = 0
   207→        self.open_time = 0.0
   208→
   209→
   210→class BudgetEnforcer:
   211→    """Enforce budget limits with soft-stop policy and circuit breaker.
   212→
   213→    Design principles:
   214→    - Non-blocking budget checks (<0.5ms, cached for 60s)
   215→    - Soft-stop: Finish current task, block new ones
   216→    - Progressive alerts at 80%, 90%, 95%
   217→    - Circuit breaker for emergency shutoff
   218→    - Graceful degradation: budget check failures don't crash the system
   219→    """
   220→
   221→    _current_instance: ClassVar[Optional["BudgetEnforcer"]] = None
   222→
   223→    def __init__(
   224→        self,
   225→        budget_usd: float,
   226→        policy: BudgetPolicy = BudgetPolicy.SOFT_STOP,
   227→        warn_threshold_pct: int = 80,
   228→        critical_threshold_pct: int = 90,
   229→        extreme_threshold_pct: int = 95,

   235→        Args:

   239→            critical_threshold_pct: Critical threshold (default: 90%)
   240→            extreme_threshold_pct: Extreme threshold (default: 95%)

   243→        """
   244→        self.budget_usd = budget_usd
   245→        self.policy = policy
   246→        self.cache_ttl_sec = cache_ttl_sec
   247→        self.vault_logger = vault_logger

   250→            warn_threshold_pct=warn_threshold_pct,
   251→            critical_threshold_pct=critical_threshold_pct,
   252→            extreme_threshold_pct=extreme_threshold_pct,
   253→        )
   254→        self.circuit_breaker = BudgetCircuitBreaker()
   255→
   256→        # Cached state (refreshed every 60s)
   257→        self._cached_state: BudgetState | None = None
   258→        self._cache_time = 0.0
   259→        self._background_tasks: set[asyncio.Task] = set()
   260→
   261→    @classmethod
   262→    def get_current(cls) -> Optional["BudgetEnforcer"]:
   263→        """Get current budget enforcer."""
   264→        return cls._current_instance
   265→
   266→    @classmethod
   267→    def set_current(cls, enforcer: Optional["BudgetEnforcer"]) -> None:
   268→        """Set current budget enforcer."""
   269→        cls._current_instance = enforcer
   270→
   271→    def check_budget(
   272→        self,
   273→        current_cost_usd: float,
   274→    ) -> tuple[bool, str]:
   275→        """Check if operation can proceed (cached, <0.5ms).
   276→
   277→        Args:
   278→            current_cost_usd: Current session cost in USD
   279→
   280→        Returns:
   281→            Tuple of (can_proceed, reason)
   282→            - can_proceed: True if within budget and policy allows
   283→            - reason: Explanation if blocked
   284→        """
   285→        # Check circuit breaker first (immediate, no cache)
   286→        if self.circuit_breaker.check_state():
   287→            return False, "Budget circuit breaker is OPEN (emergency shutoff)"
   288→
   289→        # Calculate utilization
   290→        utilization_pct = (current_cost_usd / self.budget_usd * 100) if self.budget_usd > 0 else 0
   291→
   292→        # Evaluate alerts
   293→        status, alert = self.alert_manager.evaluate(utilization_pct)
   294→
   295→        # Log alert if present (async, non-blocking)
   296→        if alert:
   297→            try:
   298→                _task = asyncio.create_task(self._log_alert_async(alert))
   299→                self._background_tasks.add(_task)
   300→                _task.add_done_callback(self._background_tasks.discard)
   301→            except RuntimeError:
   302→                # No event loop, log synchronously
   303→                logger.warning(alert)
   304→
   305→        # Apply policy
   306→        if self.policy == BudgetPolicy.SOFT_STOP and status == "BLOCKED":
   307→            # Record violation for circuit breaker
   308→            self.circuit_breaker.record_violation()
   309→            return False, f"Budget limit exceeded: {utilization_pct:.1f}%"
   310→
   311→        if self.policy == BudgetPolicy.HARD_STOP and status in (
   312→            "CRITICAL",
   313→            "EXTREME",
   314→            "BLOCKED",
   315→        ):
   316→            return False, f"Hard stop policy: {status} status ({utilization_pct:.1f}%)"
   317→
   318→        if self.policy == BudgetPolicy.WARNING_ONLY:
   319→            return True, alert or "Budget OK"
   320→
   321→        return True, f"{status}: {utilization_pct:.1f}% utilization"
   322→
   323→    async def _log_alert_async(self, alert: str) -> None:
   324→        """Log alert to vault asynchronously (best-effort)."""
   325→        if not self.vault_logger:
   326→            logger.warning(alert)
   327→            return
   328→
   329→        try:
   330→            await asyncio.wait_for(
   331→                self.vault_logger.log_alert(alert, severity="warning"),
   332→                timeout=2.0,
   333→            )
   334→        except (TimeoutError, Exception):
   335→            # Vault failure: log locally
   336→            logger.warning(f"{alert} (vault log failed)")
   337→
   338→    def get_budget_state(self, current_cost_usd: float) -> BudgetState:
   339→        """Get current budget state.
   340→
   341→        Args:
   342→            current_cost_usd: Current session cost in USD
   343→
   344→        Returns:
   345→            BudgetState snapshot
   346→        """
   347→        utilization_pct = (current_cost_usd / self.budget_usd * 100) if self.budget_usd > 0 else 0
   348→        remaining = self.budget_usd - current_cost_usd
   349→        status, _ = self.alert_manager.evaluate(utilization_pct)
   350→
   351→        return BudgetState(
   352→            total_budget_usd=self.budget_usd,
   353→            current_cost_usd=current_cost_usd,
   354→            remaining_budget_usd=remaining,
   355→            utilization_pct=utilization_pct,
   356→            status=status,
   357→            last_check_time=time.time(),
   358→            alert_count=self.alert_manager.alert_count,
   359→        )
   360→
   361→    def reset(self) -> None:
   362→        """Reset enforcer state (testing only)."""
   363→        self.alert_manager.alert_count = 0
   364→        self.alert_manager.last_warn_time = 0.0
   365→        self.alert_manager.last_critical_time = 0.0
   366→        self.circuit_breaker.reset()
   367→        self._cached_state = None
   368→        self._cache_time = 0.0
   369→
   370→
   371→def get_current_enforcer() -> BudgetEnforcer | None:
   372→    """Get current budget enforcer."""
   373→    return BudgetEnforcer.get_current()
   374→
   375→
   376→def set_current_enforcer(enforcer: BudgetEnforcer | None) -> None:
   377→    """Set current budget enforcer."""
   378→    BudgetEnforcer.set_current(enforcer)
   379→
   380→
   381→def reset_current_enforcer() -> None:
   382→    """Reset current budget enforcer (testing only)."""
   383→    BudgetEnforcer.set_current(None)
   384→

1→"""Real-time cost monitoring dashboard for multi-agent teams.
     2→
     3→Provides dashboard APIs for:
     4→- Cost aggregation by model, team, time window
     5→- Real-time spend rate ($/minute, $/hour)
     6→- Budget vs. actual tracking with alerts
     7→- Cost breakdown visualization (pie chart)
     8→- Weekly trend graphs
     9→- Integration with GlobalMetricsAggregator and BudgetEnforcer
    10→"""
    11→
    12→from __future__ import annotations
    13→
    14→import logging
    15→import time
    16→from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass, field
    17→from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any
    18→
    19→from cohezion.cost_optimization.budget_enforcer import BudgetEnforcer
    20→from cohezion.cost_optimization.cost_tracker import SessionCostTracker
    21→
    22→
    23→if TYPE_CHECKING:
    24→    from cohezion.compound.global_metrics_aggregator import GlobalMetricsAggregator
    25→
    26→
    27→logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    28→
    29→
    30→@dataclass
    31→class CostBreakdown:
    32→    """Cost breakdown by dimension (model, team, time)."""
    33→
    34→    total_cost_usd: float = 0.0
    35→    cost_by_model: dict[str, float] = field(default_factory=dict)
    36→    cost_by_team: dict[str, float] = field(default_factory=dict)
    37→    cost_by_hour: dict[str, float] = field(default_factory=dict)
    38→    tokens_by_model: dict[str, int] = field(default_factory=dict)
    39→    executions_by_model: dict[str, int] = field(default_factory=dict)
    40→
    41→    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
    42→        """Convert to dictionary for JSON serialization."""
    43→        return asdict(self)
    44→
    45→
    46→@dataclass
    47→class SpendRate:
    48→    """Real-time spend rate metrics."""
    49→
    50→    timestamp: float = field(default_factory=time.time)
    51→    spend_per_minute_usd: float = 0.0
    52→    spend_per_hour_usd: float = 0.0
    53→    spend_per_day_usd: float = 0.0
    54→    current_rate_slope: float = 0.0  # USD/minute trend
    55→    trend_direction: str = "stable"  # "increasing", "decreasing", "stable"
    56→
    57→    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
    58→        """Convert to dictionary."""
    59→        return asdict(self)
    60→
    61→
    62→@dataclass
    63→class BudgetStatus:
    64→    """Budget vs actual tracking."""
    65→
    66→    timestamp: float = field(default_factory=time.time)
    67→    total_budget_usd: float = 0.0
    68→    total_spent_usd: float = 0.0
    69→    remaining_budget_usd: float = 0.0
    70→    budget_utilization_pct: float = 0.0
    71→    budget_status: str = "healthy"  # "healthy", "warning", "critical"
    72→    hours_remaining_at_current_rate: float = 0.0
    73→    alert_level: str = "none"  # "none", "warning", "critical"
    74→
    75→    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
    76→        """Convert to dictionary."""
    77→        return asdict(self)
    78→
    79→
    80→@dataclass
    81→class TrendPoint:
    82→    """Single data point for trend graphs."""
    83→
    84→    timestamp: float
    85→    cost_usd: float
    86→    tokens: int
    87→    execution_count: int
    88→    avg_cost_per_execution: float = 0.0
    89→
    90→
    91→class CostDashboard:
    92→    """Real-time cost monitoring dashboard."""
    93→
    94→    def __init__(
    95→        self,
    96→        cost_tracker: SessionCostTracker | None = None,
    97→        budget_enforcer: BudgetEnforcer | None = None,
    98→        metrics_aggregator: GlobalMetricsAggregator | None = None,
    99→        history_window_hours: int = 24,
   100→    ):
   101→        """Initialize cost dashboard.
   102→
   103→        Args:
   104→            cost_tracker: SessionCostTracker instance (optional)
   105→            budget_enforcer: BudgetEnforcer instance (optional)
   106→            metrics_aggregator: GlobalMetricsAggregator instance (optional)
   107→            history_window_hours: Hours of history to track (default: 24)
   108→        """
   109→        self.cost_tracker = cost_tracker or SessionCostTracker.get_current()
   110→        self.budget_enforcer = budget_enforcer or BudgetEnforcer.get_current()
   111→        self.metrics_aggregator = metrics_aggregator
   112→
   113→        self.history_window_hours = history_window_hours
   114→        self.history_start_time = time.time()
   115→
   116→        # Trend history: list of (timestamp, cost, tokens, executions)
   117→        self.trend_history: list[TrendPoint] = []
   118→        self.last_aggregation_time = time.time()
   119→
   120→    def get_cost_breakdown(self, time_window_minutes: int = 60) -> CostBreakdown:
   121→        """Get cost breakdown by model, team, time window.
   122→
   123→        Args:
   124→            time_window_minutes: Time window for aggregation (default: 60 min)
   125→
   126→        Returns:
   127→            CostBreakdown with costs and tokens by dimension
   128→        """
   129→        if not self.cost_tracker:
   130→            return CostBreakdown()
   131→
   132→        # Get current session cost info
   133→        session_cost = self.cost_tracker.get_session_cost()
   134→
   135→        breakdown = CostBreakdown(
   136→            total_cost_usd=session_cost.get("total_cost_usd", 0.0),
   137→        )
   138→
   139→        # Aggregate by model from tracker history if available
   140→        if hasattr(self.cost_tracker, "model_costs"):
   141→            for model, cost in self.cost_tracker.model_costs.items():
   142→                breakdown.cost_by_model[model] = cost
   143→
   144→        if hasattr(self.cost_tracker, "token_count"):
   145→            breakdown.tokens_by_model["all_models"] = session_cost.get("total_tokens", 0)
   146→
   147→        return breakdown
   148→
   149→    def get_spend_rate(self) -> SpendRate:
   150→        """Get real-time spend rate metrics.
   151→
   152→        Returns:
   153→            SpendRate with current spend rates and trend
   154→        """
   155→        if not self.cost_tracker:
   156→            return SpendRate()
   157→
   158→        session_cost = self.cost_tracker.get_session_cost()
   159→        elapsed_minutes = max(1, (time.time() - self.history_start_time) / 60)
   160→
   161→        total_spent = session_cost.get("total_cost_usd", 0.0)
   162→        spend_per_minute = total_spent / elapsed_minutes if elapsed_minutes > 0 else 0.0
   163→
   164→        # Calculate trend from recent history
   165→        trend_direction = "stable"
   166→        if len(self.trend_history) >= 2:
   167→            recent = self.trend_history[-1]
   168→            previous = self.trend_history[-2] if len(self.trend_history) > 1 else None
   169→            if previous:
   170→                cost_change = recent.cost_usd - previous.cost_usd
   171→                if cost_change > 0.01:
   172→                    trend_direction = "increasing"
   173→                elif cost_change < -0.01:
   174→                    trend_direction = "decreasing"
   175→
   176→        return SpendRate(
   177→            spend_per_minute_usd=spend_per_minute,
   178→            spend_per_hour_usd=spend_per_minute * 60,
   179→            spend_per_day_usd=spend_per_minute * 60 * 24,
   180→            trend_direction=trend_direction,
   181→        )
   182→
   183→    def get_budget_status(self) -> BudgetStatus:
   184→        """Get budget vs actual tracking.
   185→
   186→        Returns:
   187→            BudgetStatus with budget tracking and alerts
   188→        """
   189→        if not self.budget_enforcer or not self.cost_tracker:
   190→            return BudgetStatus()
   191→
   192→        budget_usd = self.budget_enforcer.budget_usd
   193→        spent_usd = self.cost_tracker.total_cost_usd
   194→
   195→        utilization_pct = (spent_usd / budget_usd * 100) if budget_usd > 0 else 0
   196→
   197→        # Determine budget status
   198→        if utilization_pct >= 100:
   199→            budget_status = "critical"
   200→            alert_level = "critical"
   201→        elif utilization_pct >= 80:
   202→            budget_status = "warning"
   203→            alert_level = "warning"
   204→        else:
   205→            budget_status = "healthy"
   206→            alert_level = "none"
   207→
   208→        # Calculate hours remaining at current rate
   209→        spend_rate = self.get_spend_rate()
   210→        remaining_budget = max(0, budget_usd - spent_usd)
   211→        hours_remaining = (
   212→            remaining_budget / spend_rate.spend_per_hour_usd
   213→            if spend_rate.spend_per_hour_usd > 0
   214→            else float("inf")
   215→        )
   216→
   217→        return BudgetStatus(
   218→            total_budget_usd=budget_usd,
   219→            total_spent_usd=spent_usd,
   220→            remaining_budget_usd=remaining_budget,
   221→            budget_utilization_pct=utilization_pct,
   222→            budget_status=budget_status,
   223→            hours_remaining_at_current_rate=hours_remaining,
   224→            alert_level=alert_level,
   225→        )
   226→
   227→    def get_weekly_trend(self) -> list[TrendPoint]:
   228→        """Get weekly trend data for visualization.
   229→
   230→        Returns:
   231→            List of TrendPoint objects for trend graph
   232→        """
   233→        # Return trend history limited to 7 days
   234→        cutoff_time = time.time() - (7 * 24 * 60 * 60)
   235→        return [t for t in self.trend_history if t.timestamp >= cutoff_time]
   236→
   237→    def update_trend_history(self) -> None:
   238→        """Update trend history with current metrics.
   239→
   240→        Called periodically to record metrics for trend graphs.
   241→        """
   242→        if not self.cost_tracker:
   243→            return
   244→
   245→        session_cost = self.cost_tracker.get_session_cost()
   246→
   247→        point = TrendPoint(
   248→            timestamp=time.time(),
   249→            cost_usd=session_cost.get("total_cost_usd", 0.0),
   250→            tokens=session_cost.get("total_tokens", 0),
   251→            execution_count=getattr(self.cost_tracker, "execution_count", 0),
   252→        )
   253→
   254→        # Calculate average cost per execution
   255→        if point.execution_count > 0:
   256→            point.avg_cost_per_execution = point.cost_usd / point.execution_count
   257→
   258→        self.trend_history.append(point)
   259→
   260→        # Keep only recent history
   261→        cutoff_time = time.time() - (self.history_window_hours * 60 * 60)
   262→        self.trend_history = [t for t in self.trend_history if t.timestamp >= cutoff_time]
   263→
   264→    def get_cost_by_model_pie_chart(self) -> dict[str, float]:
   265→        """Get cost distribution by model for pie chart visualization.
   266→
   267→        Returns:
   268→            Dictionary of model -> percentage cost share
   269→        """
   270→        breakdown = self.get_cost_breakdown()
   271→
   272→        if not breakdown.cost_by_model or breakdown.total_cost_usd == 0:
   273→            return {}
   274→
   275→        pie_data = {}
   276→        for model, cost in breakdown.cost_by_model.items():
   277→            percentage = (cost / breakdown.total_cost_usd) * 100
   278→            pie_data[model] = percentage
   279→
   280→        return pie_data
   281→
   282→    def get_cost_forecasts(self, forecast_hours: int = 24) -> dict[str, float]:
   283→        """Get cost forecasts for next N hours.
   284→
   285→        Args:
   286→            forecast_hours: Hours to forecast (default: 24)
   287→
   288→        Returns:
   289→            Dictionary with forecast data
   290→        """
   291→        spend_rate = self.get_spend_rate()
   292→        budget_status = self.get_budget_status()
   293→
   294→        forecasts = {}
   295→        current_cost = budget_status.total_spent_usd
   296→
   297→        for hour in range(1, forecast_hours + 1):
   298→            projected_cost = current_cost + (spend_rate.spend_per_hour_usd * hour)
   299→            forecasts[f"hour_{hour}"] = projected_cost
   300→
   301→        return forecasts
   302→
   303→    def get_dashboard_summary(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
   304→        """Get complete dashboard summary for UI rendering.
   305→
   306→        Returns:
   307→            Dictionary with all dashboard metrics
   308→        """
   309→        # Update trends
   310→        self.update_trend_history()
   311→
   312→        breakdown = self.get_cost_breakdown()
   313→        spend_rate = self.get_spend_rate()
   314→        budget_status = self.get_budget_status()
   315→        pie_chart = self.get_cost_by_model_pie_chart()
   316→        weekly_trend = self.get_weekly_trend()
   317→        forecasts = self.get_cost_forecasts()
   318→
   319→        return {
   320→            "timestamp": time.time(),
   321→            "cost_breakdown": breakdown.to_dict(),
   322→            "spend_rate": spend_rate.to_dict(),
   323→            "budget_status": budget_status.to_dict(),
   324→            "cost_by_model_pie": pie_chart,
   325→            "weekly_trend": [
   326→                {
   327→                    "timestamp": t.timestamp,
   328→                    "cost_usd": t.cost_usd,
   329→                    "tokens": t.tokens,
   330→                    "executions": t.execution_count,
   331→                    "avg_cost_per_execution": t.avg_cost_per_execution,
   332→                }
   333→                for t in weekly_trend
   334→            ],
   335→            "forecasts": forecasts,
   336→        }
   337→
   338→
   339→def get_cost_dashboard() -> CostDashboard:
   340→    """Get or create singleton cost dashboard instance."""
   341→    if not hasattr(get_cost_dashboard, "_instance"):
   342→        get_cost_dashboard._instance = CostDashboard()
   343→    return get_cost_dashboard._instance
   344→
   345→
   346→def reset_cost_dashboard() -> None:
   347→    """Reset dashboard singleton (testing only)."""
   348→    if hasattr(get_cost_dashboard, "_instance"):
   349→        delattr(get_cost_dashboard, "_instance")
   350→

1→#!/usr/bin/env python3
     2→"""
     3→Obsidian Vault Helpers for AI Agents
     4→Provides CLI and Python API for Claude Code, OpenCode, Gemini CLI to interact with Obsidian.
     5→
     6→Usage:
     7→    python obsidian_helpers.py create "Note Title" --tags tag1,tag2 --related "Note1,Note2"
     8→    python obsidian_helpers.py search "query" --tags "#ai-agent"
     9→    python obsidian_helpers.py health --report
    10→    python obsidian_helpers.py daily
    11→"""
    12→
    13→import argparse
    14→import os
    15→import re
    16→import subprocess
    17→import sys
    18→from datetime import date, datetime, timedelta
    19→from pathlib import Path
    20→from typing import List, Optional
    21→
    22→
    23→class ObsidianVault:
    24→    """Python API for Obsidian vault operations."""
    25→    
    26→    def __init__(self, vault_path: Optional[str] = None):
    27→        if vault_path is None:
    28→            # Auto-detect from common locations
    29→            possible_paths = [
    30→                Path.home() / "vaults" / "cohezion-vault",
    31→                Path.home() / "Obsidian" / "cohezion-vault",
    32→                Path.cwd() / "vault",
    33→            ]
    34→            for path in possible_paths:
    35→                if path.exists():
    36→                    self.vault_path = path
    37→                    break
    38→            else:
    39→                raise FileNotFoundError(
    40→                    "Obsidian vault not found. Set vault_path or create one of:\n"
    41→                    + "\n".join(f"  - {p}" for p in possible_paths)
    42→                )
    43→        else:
    44→            self.vault_path = Path(vault_path)
    45→    
    46→    def search(self, query: str, tags: Optional[List[str]] = None, limit: int = 20) -> List[Path]:
    47→        """Search notes by text and/or tags."""
    48→        results = []
    49→        
    50→        for md_file in self.vault_path.rglob("*.md"):
    51→            if str(md_file).startswith(str(self.vault_path / ".trash")):
    52→                continue
    53→            
    54→            content = md_file.read_text()
    55→            
    56→            # Check text match
    57→            text_match = query.lower() in content.lower()
    58→            
    59→            # Check tag match
    60→            tag_match = True
    61→            if tags:
    62→                frontmatter_match = re.search(r'^---\n(.*?)\n---', content, re.DOTALL)
    63→                if frontmatter_match:
    64→                    frontmatter = frontmatter_match.group(1)
    65→                    for tag in tags:
    66→                        if tag not in frontmatter:
    67→                            tag_match = False
    68→                            break
    69→                else:
    70→                    tag_match = False
    71→            
    72→            if text_match and tag_match:
    73→                results.append(md_file.relative_to(self.vault_path))
    74→        
    75→        return sorted(results, key=lambda x: x.stat().st_mtime, reverse=True)[:limit]
    76→    
    77→    def create_note(self, 
    78→                    title: str, 
    79→                    folder: str = "concepts",
    80→                    tags: Optional[List[str]] = None,
    81→                    related: Optional[List[str]] = None,
    82→                    template: str = "standard") -> Path:
    83→        """Create a new note with frontmatter."""
    84→        # Generate slug from title
    85→        slug = re.sub(r'[^\w\s-]', '', title.lower()).strip().replace(' ', '-')
    86→        filename = f"{slug}.md"
    87→        
    88→        # Create folder if needed
    89→        folder_path = self.vault_path / folder
    90→        folder_path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    91→        
    92→        note_path = folder_path / filename
    93→        
    94→        if note_path.exists():
    95→            raise FileExistsError(f"Note already exists: {note_path}")
    96→        
    97→        # Generate frontmatter
    98→        frontmatter = [

     3→Uses the DemocraticDebate orchestrator to have multiple agent personas
     4→discuss and converge on REINFORCE hyperparameters for the FlumeNav-v0
     5→environment.

     7→
     8→import json

    11→from pathlib import Path
    12→from typing import Any

    14→from cohezion.swarm.democratic_debate import DemocraticDebate
    15→
    16→
    17→logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    18→
    19→# Sensible defaults and bounds for each hyperparameter
    20→_PARAM_SPEC: dict[str, dict[str, float]] = {
    21→    "learning_rate": {"min": 1e-5, "max": 1e-2, "default": 3e-4},
    22→    "lr": {"min": 1e-5, "max": 1e-2, "default": 3e-4},
    23→    "hidden_dim": {"min": 64, "max": 512, "default": 128},
    24→    "hidden": {"min": 64, "max": 512, "default": 128},
    25→    "gamma": {"min": 0.9, "max": 0.999, "default": 0.99},
    26→    "discount": {"min": 0.9, "max": 0.999, "default": 0.99},
    27→    "action_scale": {"min": 0.001, "max": 0.1, "default": 0.01},
    28→    "kl_weight": {"min": 1e-4, "max": 1.0, "default": 0.1},
    29→}
    30→
    31→# Canonical name mapping (aliases -> canonical)
    32→_CANONICAL: dict[str, str] = {
    33→    "lr": "learning_rate",
    34→    "hidden": "hidden_dim",
    35→    "discount": "gamma",
    36→}
    37→
    38→
    39→def _nearest_power_of_2(x: float) -> int:
    40→    """Round to nearest power of 2."""
    41→    if x <= 0:
    42→        return 64
    43→    log2 = math.log2(x)
    44→    return int(2 ** round(log2))
    45→
    46→
    47→def _clamp(value: float, lo: float, hi: float) -> float:
    48→    return max(lo, min(hi, value))
    49→
    50→
    51→def _apply_bounds(raw_params: dict[str, float]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    52→    """Clamp extracted params to sensible ranges and apply defaults."""
    53→    result: dict[str, Any] = {}
    54→
    55→    for name, value in raw_params.items():
    56→        spec = _PARAM_SPEC.get(name)
    57→        if spec is None:
    58→            continue
    59→        canonical = _CANONICAL.get(name, name)
    60→        clamped = _clamp(value, spec["min"], spec["max"])
    61→        if canonical == "hidden_dim":
    62→            clamped = float(_nearest_power_of_2(clamped))
    63→        result[canonical] = clamped
    64→
    65→    # Fill defaults for anything not extracted
    66→    defaults = {
    67→        "learning_rate": 3e-4,
    68→        "hidden_dim": 128,
    69→        "gamma": 0.99,
    70→        "action_scale": 0.01,
    71→    }
    72→    for key, default in defaults.items():
    73→        if key not in result:
    74→            result[key] = default
    75→
    76→    # Ensure hidden_dim is int in output
    77→    result["hidden_dim"] = int(result["hidden_dim"])
    78→    return result
    79→

    81→class HyperparameterDebate:
    82→    """Use democratic debate to search for RL hyperparameters."""
    83→
    84→    def __init__(self, ollama_host: str = "http://localhost:11434"):
    85→        self.ollama_host = ollama_host
    86→
    87→    async def search_rl_params(
    88→        self,
    89→        baseline_metrics: dict | None = None,
    90→        output_path: str = "data/rl/hyperparameter_debate.json",
    91→    ) -> dict:
    92→        """Run debate on RL hyperparameters, return suggested params.
    93→
    94→        Parameters
    95→        ----------
    96→        baseline_metrics
    97→            Optional dict of current training metrics to inform the debate.
    98→        output_path
    99→            Where to save the full debate session JSON.
   100→
   101→        Returns
   102→        -------
   103→        dict
   104→            Bounded hyperparameter dict with keys: learning_rate, hidden_dim,
   105→            gamma, action_scale.
   106→        """
   107→        topic = (
   108→            "Optimal REINFORCE hyperparameters for 256D FlumeNav-v0 environment, "
   109→            "CPU-only training, Hamiltonian dynamics. "
   110→            "Parameters to decide: learning_rate, hidden_dim, gamma "
   111→            "(discount factor), action_scale, reward weights."
   112→        )
   113→        if baseline_metrics:
   114→            summary = ", ".join(f"{k}={v}" for k, v in baseline_metrics.items())
   115→            topic += f" Current baseline: {summary}"
   116→
   117→        debate = DemocraticDebate(ollama_host=self.ollama_host)
   118→        try:
   119→            session = await debate.run_debate(
   120→                topic=topic,
   121→                structured_output=True,
   122→                max_rounds=3,
   123→                min_rounds=3,
   124→            )
   125→        finally:
   126→            await debate.close()
   127→
   128→        # Extract params from the consensus
   129→        raw_params: dict[str, float] = {}
   130→        if session.final_consensus:
   131→            raw_params = session.final_consensus.get("extracted_params", {})
   132→
   133→        params = _apply_bounds(raw_params)
   134→
   135→        # Save full session
   136→        out = Path(output_path)
   137→        out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   138→        with open(out, "w") as f:

   146→                default=str,
   147→            )
   148→        logger.info("Hyperparameter debate saved to %s", out)

   150→        return params

    59→        data_dir : str

    75→        if kl_weight is not None:
    76→            config.kl_weight = kl_weight
    77→        config.epochs = additional_epochs
    78→        config.data_dir = data_dir
    79→

    82→        metrics_path = trainer.metrics_path
    83→        if metrics_path.exists():

    93→        metrics = trainer.train()

   109→        ckpt_files = sorted(ckpt_dir.glob("flume_vae_ep*.pt"))
   110→        latest_ckpt = str(ckpt_files[-1]) if ckpt_files else ""
   111→
   112→        logger.info(
   113→            "Incremental VAE: %d epochs, total_loss %.4f → %.4f (%s)",
   114→            additional_epochs,
   115→            baseline_total,
   116→            final["total"],
   117→            "improved" if improved else "no improvement",
   118→        )
   119→
   120→        return IncrementalResult(
   121→            iteration=0,
   122→            epochs_trained=len(metrics),

   124→            checkpoint_path=latest_ckpt,

   126→        )
   127→
   128→
   129→class IncrementalRLTrainer:
   130→    """Resume RL training from a policy checkpoint with new hyperparameters.
   131→
   132→    Parameters
   133→    ----------
   134→    checkpoint_path : str or Path
   135→        Path to the policy checkpoint to resume from.
   136→    """
   137→
   138→    def __init__(self, checkpoint_path: str | Path) -> None:
   139→        self.checkpoint_path = Path(checkpoint_path)
   140→
   141→    def train_more(
   142→        self,
   143→        additional_episodes: int = 100,
   144→        lr: float | None = None,
   145→        gamma: float | None = None,
   146→        hidden_dim: int = 128,
   147→        output_dir: str = "data/rl/checkpoints",
   148→    ) -> IncrementalResult:
   149→        """Train additional episodes from the checkpoint.
   150→
   151→        Parameters
   152→        ----------
   153→        additional_episodes : int
   154→            Number of new episodes to train.
   155→        lr : float, optional
   156→            Override learning rate.
   157→        gamma : float, optional
   158→            Override discount factor.
   159→        hidden_dim : int
   160→            Hidden layer dimension (must match checkpoint).
   161→        output_dir : str
   162→            Directory for output checkpoints.
   163→
   164→        Returns
   165→        -------
   166→        IncrementalResult
   167→            Result including whether coherence improved.
   168→        """
   169→        import gymnasium as gym
   170→        import torch
   171→
   172→        from cohezion.rl.trainer import PolicyNetwork, TrainingConfig
   173→
   174→        # Load existing policy
   175→        state_dict = torch.load(self.checkpoint_path, map_location="cpu", weights_only=True)
   176→        h, s = state_dict["shared.0.weight"].shape
   177→        a = state_dict["mean_head.weight"].shape[0]
   178→
   179→        policy = PolicyNetwork(s, a, h)
   180→        policy.load_state_dict(state_dict)
   181→
   182→        config = TrainingConfig(
   183→            n_episodes=additional_episodes,
   184→            lr=lr or 3e-4,
   185→            gamma=gamma or 0.99,
   186→            z_dim=s,
   187→            hidden_dim=h,
   188→            output_dir=output_dir,
   189→        )
   190→
   191→        env = gym.make("cohezion/FlumeNav-v0", max_steps=config.max_steps)
   192→        optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(policy.parameters(), lr=config.lr)
   193→
   194→        coherences: list[float] = []
   195→        rewards: list[float] = []
   196→
   197→        for ep in range(additional_episodes):
   198→            obs, info = env.reset(seed=ep + 10000)
   199→            ep_rewards: list[float] = []
   200→            log_probs: list[torch.Tensor] = []
   201→            ep_coherences: list[float] = []
   202→
   203→            for _ in range(config.max_steps):

   206→                ep_rewards.append(reward)
   207→                log_probs.append(log_prob)

   211→
   212→            # REINFORCE update
   213→            returns: list[float] = []
   214→            g = 0.0
   215→            for r in reversed(ep_rewards):
   216→                g = r + config.gamma * g
   217→                returns.insert(0, g)
   218→            returns_t = torch.FloatTensor(returns)
   219→            if len(returns_t) > 1:
   220→                returns_t = (returns_t - returns_t.mean()) / (returns_t.std() + 1e-8)
   221→
   222→            loss = torch.tensor(0.0)
   223→            for lp, ret in zip(log_probs, returns_t, strict=False):
   224→                loss = loss - lp * ret
   225→            optimizer.zero_grad()
   226→            loss.backward()
   227→            torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(policy.parameters(), 1.0)
   228→            optimizer.step()
   229→

   231→            rewards.append(sum(ep_rewards))

   235→        # Save updated policy

   237→        out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   238→        save_path = out_dir / "policy_final.pt"
   239→        torch.save(policy.state_dict(), save_path)
   240→
   241→        avg_coh = float(np.mean(coherences[-50:])) if coherences else 0.0
   242→        avg_reward = float(np.mean(rewards[-50:])) if rewards else 0.0
   243→

    44→### 1. Prepare Execution Context

    55→const parseBooleanFlag = (value, defaultValue = true) => {
    56→  if (typeof value === 'string') {
    57→    const normalized = value.trim().toLowerCase();
    58→    if (['false', '0', 'off', 'no'].includes(normalized)) return false;
    59→    if (['true', '1', 'on', 'yes'].includes(normalized)) return true;
    60→  }
    61→  if (value === undefined || value === null) return defaultValue;
    62→  return Boolean(value);

    77→  },

    87→const normalizeUserExecutionMode = (mode) => {
    88→  if (typeof mode !== 'string') return null;
    89→  const normalized = mode.trim().toLowerCase().replace(/[-_]/g, ' ').replace(/\s+/g, ' ');
    90→

    92→  if (normalized === 'sequential') return 'sequential';
    93→  if (normalized === 'subagent' || normalized === 'sub agent' || normalized === 'subagents' || normalized === 'sub agents') {
    94→    return 'subagent';
    95→  }
    96→  if (normalized === 'agent team' || normalized === 'agent teams' || normalized === 'agentteam') {
    97→    return 'agent-team';
    98→  }
    99→
   100→  return null;
   101→};
   102→
   103→const normalizeConfigExecutionMode = (mode) => {
   104→  if (mode === 'subagent') return 'subagent';
   105→  if (mode === 'auto' || mode === 'sequential' || mode === 'subagent' || mode === 'agent-team') {
   106→    return mode;
   107→  }
   108→  return null;
   109→};
   110→
   111→// Explicit user instruction in the active run takes priority over config.
   112→const explicitModeFromUser = normalizeUserExecutionMode(runtime.getExplicitExecutionModeHint?.() || null);
   113→
   114→const requestedMode = explicitModeFromUser || normalizeConfigExecutionMode(subagentContext.config.execution_mode) || 'auto';
   115→const probeEnabled = subagentContext.config.capability_probe;
   116→
   117→const supports = {
   118→  subagent: false,
   119→  agentTeam: false,

   125→  supports.agentTeam = runtime.canLaunchAgentTeams?.() === true;
   126→}
   127→
   128→let resolvedMode = requestedMode;
   129→
   130→if (requestedMode === 'auto') {
   131→  if (supports.agentTeam) resolvedMode = 'agent-team';
   132→  else if (supports.subagent) resolvedMode = 'subagent';
   133→  else resolvedMode = 'sequential';
   134→} else if (probeEnabled && requestedMode === 'agent-team' && !supports.agentTeam) {
   135→  resolvedMode = supports.subagent ? 'subagent' : 'sequential';
   136→} else if (probeEnabled && requestedMode === 'subagent' && !supports.subagent) {
   137→  resolvedMode = 'sequential';
   138→}
   139→
   140→subagentContext.execution = {
   141→  requestedMode,
   142→  resolvedMode,
   143→  probeEnabled,
   144→  supports,
   145→};
   146→```

   149→
   150→1. Explicit user request in this run (`agent team` => `agent-team`; `subagent` => `subagent`; `sequential`; `auto`)
   151→2. `tea_execution_mode` from config
   152→3. Runtime capability fallback (when probing enabled)
